$comment: INTENDED lifecycle rules for the B2 archive bucket. Changing a number here is
a reviewable change; changing it in the Backblaze console is not, which is the
whole point of committing it.
WHY THESE NUMBERS ARE NOT EXPLAINED HERE. The ceilings, the floors, and the
reasoning that fixes each value live in scripts/lifecycle-policy.mjs — the one
module BOTH writers (apply-bucket-lifecycle.mjs and setup-backblaze.mjs) must
pass through, and the only copy a mechanical check can reach. An earlier
revision of this comment asserted that reasoning was not duplicated here while
carrying a full copy of it, and three review rounds each corrected one copy of
the same sentence before the duplication itself was treated as the defect
(#1471 r6/r7/r8). One of those edits also truncated a sentence mid-clause,
which is what a second copy costs.
WHAT YOU DO NEED TO KNOW READING THIS FILE:
- Worst-case object lifetime is the SUM of both terms per prefix, because a
version is deleted `daysFromHidingToDeleting` after it is hidden, and it is
hidden either by the age rule OR by being superseded at the same key.
Reasoning about the first term alone is the mistake that once put the live
bucket at a 60-day daily worst case.
- The recovery window is an UPPER BOUND, not a guarantee per incident.
`daysFromHidingToDeleting` counts from when a version became non-current,
and the age rule hiding it counts — so a version hidden by age on day 20 is
deleted on day 29 regardless, and an overwrite on day 28 leaves about one
day, not nine. It decays to zero as a version nears its deletion date, and
within a promise-capped lifetime that decay cannot be designed away. See
lifecycle-policy.mjs for why it is still worth having (the newest archive,
which is what a restore reaches for, is current and gets the full window).
- Both sums are capped by PUBLISHED PRIVACY PROMISES (PrivacyPolicy.md and
the rendered privacy page), not by preference. They are facts about the
product. lifecycle-policy.mjs refuses a declaration that breaches either.
- The yearly prefixes deliberately get NO rule; that absence is what gives
them indefinite retention.
Verify against live with `npm run bucket:lifecycle:print`; check for drift with
`npm run bucket:lifecycle:check`.
